title: Exactness at the middle first Tor module of a short exact sequence
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A,B,C,M$ be $R$-modules, and let $0\to A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}C\to0$ be short exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. For the Tor modules and functorial maps of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], the sequence $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(A,M)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tor}_1(u,M)}\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(B,M)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,M)}\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(C,M)$ is exact at its middle term: the kernel of the second map equals the image of the first. No flatness, finiteness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00M0, lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor: the three consecutive degree-one Tor terms, with the two module arguments exchanged by Tor symmetry.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split] to the given short exact sequence. Obtain free resolutions $P_\bullet,Q_\bullet,S_\bullet$ of $A,B,C$, with augmentation-compatible chain maps $a:P_\bullet\to Q_\bullet$ and $b:Q_\bullet\to S_\bullet$ lifting $u,v$, and degreewise splitting maps $p_n:Q_n\to P_n$, $s_n:S_n\to Q_n$ satisfying $b_na_n=0$, $p_na_n=1$, $b_ns_n=1$ and $a_np_n+s_nb_n=1$. These choices impose no condition on $M$.

source.place: Tag 065P, lemma-reverse-long-exact-seq-ext, proof: construction of the degreewise split sequence of free resolutions.

proof.text: Put $X_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_RM$, $Y_\bullet=Q_\bullet\otimes_RM$, $Z_\bullet=S_\bullet\otimes_RM$, and $f=a\otimes1_M$, $g=b\otimes1_M$. Tensor the splitting maps as well. The four identities of step 1 persist, since $(h\otimes1)(k\otimes1)=(hk)\otimes1$ and $(h+k)\otimes1=h\otimes1+k\otimes1$, as checked on $x\otimes m$. Hence $f_n$ is injective, $g_n$ is surjective, and $g_ny=0$ implies $y=f_n((p_n\otimes1)y)$. Thus $0\to X_n\to Y_n\to Z_n\to0$ is exact in every degree, even when $M$ is not flat. The chain-map equations for $a,b$ give those for $f,g$ by the same composition identity.

source.place: Tag 065P, lemma-reverse-long-exact-seq-ext, degreewise splitting argument, applied to tensor instead of Hom; explicit elementary tensor identities.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian] to work in the abelian category of $R$-modules. Reindex each nonnegative chain complex as an integer cochain complex: set $\widetilde X^{-n}=X_n$ for $n\ge0$, with the same differentials, and $\widetilde X^i=0$ for $i>0$, and likewise for $Y,Z,f,g$. The sequence remains short exact in each degree; in positive degrees it is the zero sequence. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] in degree $-1$. Since $H^{-1}(\widetilde X)=\ker(d_{X,1})/\operatorname{im}(d_{X,2})=H_1(X_\bullet)$, and the induced maps are unchanged on these quotients, it gives exactness of $H_1(X_\bullet)\xrightarrow{H_1(f)}H_1(Y_\bullet)\xrightarrow{H_1(g)}H_1(Z_\bullet)$ at the middle term.

source.place: Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain, the horizontal degree-i sequence, with i=-1.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], the chosen free resolutions give canonical isomorphisms $\iota_A:\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(A,M)\to H_1(X_\bullet)$, $\iota_B:\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(B,M)\to H_1(Y_\bullet)$ and $\iota_C:\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(C,M)\to H_1(Z_\bullet)$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift], applied to the augmentation-compatible lifts $a,b$, gives $\iota_B\operatorname{Tor}_1(u,M)=H_1(f)\iota_A$ and $\iota_C\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,M)=H_1(g)\iota_B$. If $t$ lies in the kernel of $\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,M)$, step 3 gives $x\in H_1(X_\bullet)$ with $H_1(f)x=\iota_Bt$, and then $t=\operatorname{Tor}_1(u,M)(\iota_A^{-1}x)$. Conversely $H_1(g)H_1(f)=0$, so the same two identities and injectivity of $\iota_C$ show that every image element lies in that kernel. This proves the asserted equality of kernel and image.
